text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • P1 • us-west-2 inference cluster
incident-bot: Summary: multiple inference pods experiencing CUDA OOMs despite reported headroom. Node-level container restarts and degraded 5xx rate to customers (~2.4% of prod traffic). Auto-attach oncall.

Eric (oncall): ack — I'm jumping in. First pass, what's the blast radius?

Anna SRE: seeing ~12 pods across 3 nodes hitting OOMs over the last 4m. Pod logs show allocator reservation attempts followed by cudaErrorOutOfMemory. Host memory spikes around the same time (swap activity + kernel pagefaults).

Miguel (eng-runtime): curious — telemetry shows headroom metric on runtime agent still ~900MB per pod before the OOM. So we have headroom reported but CUDA OOMs anyway. Suspect fragmentation + pinned reserved blocks + aggressive KV prefetch.

Lewis (observability): alert window: 2026-03-15T14:32:10Z -> now. 503s spiked to 2.4% for generation endpoints, tail latency increased. Top affected model: rwinf-13b-v2 quantized variant. Customers impacted: a subset of PLG traffic (no enterprise SLA customers reported yet) — CS loop opened.

Janet (Customer Success): I've started outreach to the top 5 highest-usage tenants; they saw brief failures and auto-retry handled most. We'll update if any customers escalate.

Eric (oncall): steps to mitigate? Can we reduce memory churn or disable prefetch quickly?

Miguel (eng-runtime): yes. Two quick knobs: 1) disable KV prefetch (this reduces caches filling reserved blocks), 2) drop allocator soft-reserve so runtime doesn't hold large reserved slabs. I'll propose commands below.

Miguel (eng-runtime): quick mitigation plan (low-risk, reversible):
- Flip runtime flag disable_prefetch=true on affected deployment(s)
- Set ALLOC_SOFT_RESERVE=0 for pods temporarily
- Restart pods one node at a time to avoid capacity loss

Miguel (eng-runtime): example kubectl patch for the deployment (one namespace at a time):
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch deployment rwinf-13b-deploy --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"ALLOC_SOFT_RESERVE","value":"0"}}]'
# then update configmap for prefetch
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/rwinf-13b-deploy DISABLE_KV_PREFETCH=true
```

Anna SRE: applying to one node first. Doing a rolling restart of the rwinf-13b-deploy on node-az1 (cordon + drain + uncordon). Will keep concurrency at 1/3 during restart.

infra-bot: node node-az1 cordoned by Anna SRE at 14:37:05Z

Eric (oncall): monitor memory + kernel logs during restart. Lewis, can you surface per-pod reserved-block metrics and fragmentation indices?

Lewis (observability): on it — querying allocator reserve histogram and fragmentation_ratio for the pods in that node. Sending graphs to thread in 30s.

Lewis (observability): posted graphs — fragmentation_ratio jumps to 0.78 before OOMs; reserved_block_count also spikes. When we flip disable_prefetch, reserved_block_count trends down to baseline within ~45s per pod.

Miguel (eng-runtime): that matches: prefetch creates many small cached tensors that get pinned in GPU address space + sparsely allocated slab meta causes fragmentation. With soft reserve >0 runtime holds larger reserved slabs making fragmentation visible as effective free memory << headroom_metric (headroom is free continuous region, not accounting for fragmentation).

Anna SRE: second pod in node drained and restarted, no immediate OOM. Latency for that pod temporarily up due to cold KV cache but stable. Rolling to next node.

Janet (Customer Success): Slack update prepared for customers — neutral tone: "We experienced transient errors for some generation calls in us-west-2; mitigation applied and services are recovering. Our team will follow up if you saw persistent errors." Want to send now or wait for full recovery?

Eric (oncall): wait until we confirm <0.5% 5xxs for 15m. Then send. Keep CS draft in thread.

Miguel (eng-runtime): follow-up fix candidates (medium-term):
- Rework allocator to avoid large contiguous reserved slabs for quantized models; move to smaller slab sizes + best-fit fallback
- Introduce a fragmentation-aware headroom metric (continuous vs fragmented free space)
- Throttle KV prefetch pressure based on fragmentation signal

Miguel (eng-runtime): short-term patch I'll push after stabilization: decrease DEFAULT_SLAB_SIZE from 256MB -> 64MB behind a rollout flag.

Anna SRE: continuing roll — node-az2 next. We'll keep at most one node drained at a time.

infra-bot: node node-az2 cordoned at 14:42:53Z

Lewis (observability): 5xx rate falling: 1.6% -> 0.7% since first restarts started. Fragmentation trending downward across rolling pods.

Eric (oncall): good. Any pods still flapping or OOMing?

Anna SRE: one pod on node-az3 had repeated OOMs even after flags (looks like leftover pinned blocks from previous runtime version). I'm evicting it and forcing a node-level reclaim (dropping caches) before re-scheduling.

Anna SRE: command run on node-az3:
```bash
kubectl delete pod rwinf-13b-7f8c9 --namespace=inference --grace-period=0 --force
ssh node-az3 sudo sh -c "echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches"
```

Miguel (eng-runtime): that node-level reclaim helped in canary yesterday. Good call.

Janet (Customer Success): CS draft ready — I'll send after Eric confirms green. Also collecting any tenant error logs if they want details.

Eric (oncall): monitoring 15m. Lewis, please post a final metric snapshot at 14:55Z.

Lewis (observability): final snapshot at 14:55:10Z - 5xx rate 0.32%, fragmentation median 0.28, reserved_block_count down to baseline. No crashed pods in last 7 minutes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • mitigation applied: disable_prefetch + ALLOC_SOFT_RESERVE=0 + rolling restarts. Status: service recovering.

Miguel (eng-runtime): I'll cut a canary change to DEFAULT_SLAB_SIZE flag today and coordinate with Anna for a controlled rollout tomorrow. Also opening a ticket to implement fragmentation-aware headroom.

Anna SRE: As follow-ups: create postmortem, add a runbook entry for "CUDA OOM despite headroom" with quick mitigation steps (disable prefetch, reduce reserve, drain strategy), and add alert for fragmentation_ratio > 0.6.

Janet (Customer Success): Sending customer note now — will CC svc-alerts.

Eric (oncall): closing the incident channel in 30 mins if metrics stay good. Assigning postmortem to Miguel + Anna. Thanks all.

Miguel (eng-runtime): will own root-cause writeup. Immediate action items: rollback prefetch throttle if stable, schedule allocator refactor. ETA for patch: 48-72h.

Anna SRE: leaving a few links in the ticket: kernel OOM logs, pod logs snippet, and the kubectl commands we ran. Will detail the node reclaim step.

Lewis (observability): saved dashboard and added temporary annotation for the incident window.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED • follow-ups required: allocator refactor, fragmentation headroom metric, runbook update, postmortem due in 3d.
